title: Apple Announces September 9 Product Launch
main_content:
The rumors continue to swirl about Apple’s upcoming iPhone6.

The world’s third-largest mobile phone maker is hosting a product launch in Cupertino, California, September 9. Apple has teased the buying public in its event invitations by claiming, “Wish we could say more.”

Online technology websites are convinced that Apple may reveal a new generation iPhone with a bigger screen. Apple watchers say the existing 10-centimeter display will be widened to nearly 12 centimeters.

The sites also talk about the possibility of an iWatch, a smartwatch that could help monitor people’s health and control Internet-connected appliances and electronics in the home. If the technology sites prove true, the release would be the company’s first new product launch since the iPad in 2010.

Apple has since redesigned and added features to its iPhones, iPads, iPods and the Mac since the release of the iPad. Those moves have raised concerns among investors that the company has lacked new ideas since the October 2011 death of chief visionary Steve Jobs.

questions.question: How did Apple advertise their new launch?
options: Through a press conference in San Francisco.
By sending out personalized invitations to top customers.
By teasing the public with an ambiguous message in event invitations.
With a major social media campaign featuring countdowns.
questions.answer: By teasing the public with an ambiguous message in event invitations.

questions.question: What are specialists assuming the launch will be about?
options: The introduction of an advanced laptop model.
The unveiling of a new generation iPhone and possibly an iWatch.
A significant update to the Mac operating system.
An expansion of Apple's cloud services platform.
questions.answer: The unveiling of a new generation iPhone and possibly an iWatch.

questions.question: What concerns have investors expressed towards Apple?
options: The company is losing market share to smaller competitors.
Apple has not launched any new products since 2010.
There is a perceived lack of innovation following Steve Jobs' death.
The quality of Apple's current product lineup is declining.
questions.answer: There is a perceived lack of innovation following Steve Jobs' death.
